encounters.cc: Generalized weakness, right arm pain, and unexplained bruising in the setting of advanced dementia

lines: Generalized weakness, right arm pain, and unexplained bruising in the setting of advanced dementia

The patient is a 78-year-old female with vascular dementia, residual right-sided hemiparesis, and a history of recurrent pressure ulcers including Stage III sacral involvement documented in prior encounters.
She returns to the emergency department accompanied by her son with complaints of generalized weakness and pain in her right arm.
She is reluctant to explain how she got these bruises and looks toward her son before answering any questions.
Her son reports that she is often clumsy and falls because she refuses to use her walker.
